question.problem: The shoulder height of a moose $h$ measures $2.1\,\text{m}$ to the nearest tenth of a meter. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.
question.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{m}}{2}=0.05\,\text{m}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =2.1\,\text{m}-0.05\,\text{m} \\  & =2.05\,\text{m} \\ \text{upper bound} & =2.1\,\text{m}+0.05\,\text{m} \\  & =2.15\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $h$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
2.05\,\text{m}\le h<2.15\,\text{m}.
$$
